blocks.html: High-level modules should not reference or construct low-level classes directly.
blocks.text: High-level modules should not reference or construct low-level classes directly.

blocks.html:
Check: Search for
new
statements or direct imports of infrastructure code inside high-level logic. If found, DIP is violated.

If you see:
HighLevel → ConcreteDatabase
, DIP is broken.

blocks.html: Both high-level and low-level modules must rely on an interface or abstract class.

blocks.html: Check: Identify if both layers depend on the same abstraction rather than each other’s concrete code.

blocks.html: Dependency Inversion Principle is called “inversion” because it reverses the traditional direction of source code dependencies — low-level implementation details now depend on high-level policy abstractions instead of the high-level depending on low-level implementations.
